title: Open a backfilled tube furnace safely and load a boat of chips under its thermocouple
instruction: Take the end cap off while the gauge is in its green band and shut the gas, lift the lid, push the boat under the thermocouple while holding the tube, then put everything back.
context: Loading a tube furnace is daily work in materials labs. The cap may only come off in the gauge's safe band, and the loose quartz tube must be held while the boat goes in.
setup: A bench with the two arms' bases at x = 0, y = +0.30 and -0.30 m (x points away from them; heights are above the bench). A compact split-tube furnace, white steel, 410 mm wide (y = -0.125 to 0.285 m), 280 mm deep (x = 0.215 to 0.495 m), 360 mm high: a 110 mm base with the controller (its screen reads 28, in degrees C), the heated lower half, and a lid hinged along the back at 220 mm that lifts by a handle bar on its front (y = 0.20 to 0.28 m, 280 mm high); a thermocouple's tip stands beside the tube at the hot zone's centre, y = 0.08 m. Across it, in the gap between the halves, a loose fused-quartz tube, 25.4 mm outside, 22 mm inside, 610 mm long, axis at x = 0.355 m, 220 mm high, from y = -0.225 m (its open end, by the right arm) to 0.385 m, resting on two saddles in the furnace's end walls. At its far end a stainless fitting carries a compound gauge facing the arms (-20 to +20 kPa, green from 2 to 8 kPa, red above); in front of it the gas valve stands on its own post, a quarter-turn ball valve whose red lever points at the arms (open). The near end is shut by an aluminium quick-release cap (60 g: a 5 mm plate, a 25 mm sleeve, 36.4 mm across). In the tube, just inside the cap, an alumina boat 80 x 15 x 8 mm, 20 g, its back end a 12 mm tab, holds three 8 x 8 x 0.5 mm silicon chips in a row, 24 mm apart. In line with the tube a stainless hook rod, 6 mm round, 390 mm, 90 g, with a 10 mm pusher disc, lies on two rests (y = -0.30 and -0.52 m) with its pusher at y = -0.27 m. A stand for the cap is at x = 0.25 m, y = -0.27 m. The gas is on at the start: the gauge reads 1 kPa and rises 0.4 kPa per second while the cap is on and the valve open.
scoring: 0 if at any time: the cap comes off while the gauge reads under 2 kPa; the gauge goes over 8 kPa; the valve stays open more than 5 s after the cap is off; a chip moves over 3 mm on the boat or tilts over 30 degrees; the boat tilts over 20 degrees; the tube moves over 3 mm or turns over 3 degrees. 0 also unless the boat, chips, rod, cap and lid have moved under 1 mm over the last second, and unless the boat's centre is within 8 mm of the thermocouple along the tube. Otherwise 0.2, plus 0.2 each for: the rod on its rests within 15 mm of where it started; the lid shut (within 2 degrees); the cap home and square (plate within 2 mm of the tube's end, axis within 3 mm and 3 degrees of the tube's) with the valve shut. 1.0 if all three, and every fingertip is at least 8 cm from the rod, the cap and the lid's handle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim. The gas is a model: pressure rises at a set rate with the valve open and the cap on; the gauge shows it. The pressure's hold on the cap and the O-ring are not simulated; the green band is a scoring rule. The tube's wall is 16-sided with a smooth floor strip; the lid's stiff hinge is a drive that holds it where it is left. No heat.
